name: United Kingdom
note: The United Kingdom in the style of the Russian model tree: democratic government as the historical path and alternatives led by real parties of the data; economy (public services, the bank rescue, austerity, HS2, offshore wind), the union and the constitution (Northern Ireland, the Scottish referendum, leaving the EU), defence (the 2010 review, Trident, AUKUS). Sourced starting spirits in data/spirits/gbr.json. Alternatives are a counterfactual.

source.title: Wikipedia: Strategic Defence and Security Review 2010

focuses.name: The direction of the country
focuses.description: Which camp governs the country.

focuses.name: Democratic government
focuses.description: Parties alternate in power through elections, as they historically did.

focuses.name: A turn to the left
focuses.description: Parties of the left (Labour) gain on wages, welfare and public services.

focuses.name: Unions and voters
focuses.description: Unions and young voters rally to the left.

focuses.name: A left-wing government
focuses.description: The most popular party of the democratic left leads the government.

focuses.name: Expand the welfare state
focuses.description: Public health care and higher pensions.

focuses.name: A liberal turn
focuses.description: Liberal parties (the Liberal Democrats) gain ground on reform and civil liberties.

focuses.name: Reform agenda
focuses.description: A programme of deregulation and civil liberties.

focuses.name: A liberal government
focuses.description: The most popular liberal party leads the government.

focuses.name: Liberal reforms
focuses.description: Cut red tape and open markets.

focuses.name: A conservative turn
focuses.description: Conservative parties (the Conservatives and the Ulster Unionists) gain on order, tax cuts and tradition.

focuses.name: Business and the countryside
focuses.description: Business and rural voters rally to the right.

focuses.name: A conservative government
focuses.description: The most popular conservative party leads the government.

focuses.name: Fiscal discipline
focuses.description: Cut spending and taxes to balance the budget.

focuses.name: A populist wave
focuses.description: National-populist parties (UKIP, the Brexit Party and later Reform UK) gain on immigration and sovereignty.

focuses.name: Rallies and referendums
focuses.description: Mass rallies and calls for referendums.

focuses.name: A national-populist government
focuses.description: The most popular national-populist party leads the government.

focuses.name: Sovereignty first
focuses.description: Restrict immigration and limit the power of international bodies.

focuses.name: A socialist turn
focuses.description: Socialist and communist parties (Respect) gain in a crisis.

focuses.name: Strikes and occupations
focuses.description: Strikes and workplace occupations.

focuses.name: A socialist government
focuses.description: The most popular socialist party leads the government.

focuses.name: Public ownership
focuses.description: Nationalise the banks and the largest companies.

focuses.name: Economic agenda
focuses.description: Priorities for the British economy.

focuses.name: Invest in public services
focuses.description: More money for schools and hospitals.

focuses.name: The City of London
focuses.description: Keep London a global financial centre.

focuses.name: Rescue the banks
focuses.description: Nationalise failing banks such as Northern Rock in the financial crisis.

focuses.name: Austerity
focuses.description: Cut spending to close the deficit after the crisis.

focuses.name: Fintech
focuses.description: Make Britain a centre for financial technology.

focuses.name: High Speed 2
focuses.description: A new high-speed railway from London to the north, under construction since 2020.

focuses.name: Offshore wind
focuses.description: The largest offshore wind fleet in the world. Unlocks new wind farms.

focuses.name: Levelling up
focuses.description: Investment in the poorer regions of the north and the Midlands.

focuses.name: New nuclear plants
focuses.description: New reactors at Hinkley Point and Sizewell.

focuses.name: The union and the constitution
focuses.description: Devolution, Northern Ireland and Europe.

focuses.name: Power sharing in Northern Ireland
focuses.description: Keep the institutions of the Good Friday Agreement working.

focuses.name: The Scottish referendum
focuses.description: Hold a referendum on Scottish independence; on 18 September 2014 Scotland voted No by 55.3 to 44.7 percent.

focuses.name: Leave the European Union
focuses.description: The United Kingdom left the European Union on 31 January 2020.

focuses.name: New trade deals
focuses.description: Trade agreements with Australia, Japan and the Pacific partnership.

focuses.name: A new devolution settlement
